title: Our Free Apps | Apps for Change
description: Goal Getter, Care About You, Beat the Craving, and Advocate's Compass: four free, private apps from a Minnesota nonprofit, coming in 2027.
headline: Our apps
body: Four free apps for four parts of a good life: growing toward your goals, caring for others, staying strong when cravings hit, and speaking up for yourself. All four are coming to iPhone and Android in 2027.

sections.heading: Every app makes the same promises

items: Free forever. No ads, subscriptions, or in-app purchases.
Your information is stored securely in your account, so it's there when you get a new phone.
We never sell your data or share it with employers, insurers, funders, or partner organizations.
You can delete your entries or your whole account at any time.

title: Goal Getter | Apps for Change
description: Goal Getter helps you set goals for every part of your life, break them into small steps, and see where you're thriving and where you need a little more care.
headline: Your whole life, one clear view.
body: You're juggling work, family, money, health, and maybe a dream you keep putting off. Goal Getter helps you set goals for every part of your life, break them into small steps, and see where you're thriving and where you need a little more care.
label: Goal Getter · Coming 2027
tagline: Free. No ads. Never sold. Built by a nonprofit, for you.

items: Your to-do list is long, but the things that matter most keep slipping.
You're doing well at work, but your friendships, health, or peace of mind are running on empty.
You've tried goal apps before, but tracking one habit at a time never showed you the bigger picture.

blocks.text: You don't need to do more. You need to see your life clearly and take the next right step. That's what Goal Getter is for.

sections.heading: Twelve areas of a balanced life

blocks.text: Most goal apps focus on one habit at a time. Goal Getter grew out of our founding framework of eight areas of a balanced life. As we built it, we saw that a full life needed even more room, so the eight grew into twelve:
Physical · Emotional · Spiritual · Intellectual · Occupational · Financial · Social · Relationships · Hobbies · Leisure · Service · Environmental
Each area has its own color, so you can see at a glance where your energy is going. New to the framework? Tap the Life Areas tab to learn what each area means and why it matters.

items: Explore your life areas. Start by reading about the twelve areas and thinking about which ones you want to grow.
Set your first goal. Name what you want, choose its life area, and break it into action steps and milestones you can actually do.
Put it on your calendar. Give each step a date so it fits into real life. Your steps, milestones, and due dates show up on the Goal Getter calendar, and you can add them to your phone's calendar too.
See the whole picture. Open your dashboard to see every goal, every area, and what needs your attention next.

blocks.text: Today's Updates
Start each day knowing exactly what's on your plate: today's tasks, upcoming due dates, progress updates, and milestones you've reached.
Top Goals
Keep the goals that matter most front and center so they don't get lost in a busy week.
Find Your Balance

Twelve colored blocks, one for each life area, show how many goals you've set in each. If an area has no goals yet, it lights up yellow with a star, a gentle nudge that this part of your life could use some attention.

items: Reminders that fit your schedule. Check-ins come when they're helpful, not overwhelming.
Reflections. Write a few short notes on what's working and what you'd change. Small insights add up.
Celebrate your milestones. Every win shows up in Today's Updates, and if you'd like, Goal Getter will email you a note to celebrate it.

blocks.text: “Taking a holistic approach to my own goals changed my life. Looking at every area, not just work or money, led me to more meaningful relationships, a healthier outlook, and the courage to start this nonprofit. I built Goal Getter so anyone can have that same clear view of their life, for free.”

title: Care About You | Apps for Change
description: Be the friend you mean to be. Care About You helps you turn good intentions into small, real acts of kindness for the people in your life and for yourself.
headline: Be the friend you mean to be.
body: You think about the people you love all the time. You mean to call, send that note, or finally get coffee. Then the week fills up, and another month goes by. Care About You helps you turn those good intentions into small, real acts of kindness for the people in your life and for yourself.
label: Care About You · Coming 2027

blocks.text: Free. No ads. Never sold. Built by a nonprofit, for you.
Get launch updates
Become a private tester

items: You keep meaning to text that friend back. It's been three months.
You remember the birthday the day after.
Most of your conversations lately have been about logistics, not connection.
You take care of everyone else and forget to take care of yourself.

blocks.text: You're not a bad friend. You're busy. Care About You makes it easier to show up.

items: Choose who it's for. Plan something kind for someone in your life, or for yourself.
Pick what you'll do. Choose an action: coffee, lunch, dinner, a call, a walk, a written note, a compliment, a gift, help around the house, offering support, or something of your own.
Add a note if you'd like. A few words to remember why it matters.
Pick a day and time. Your plan shows up on your dashboard, and you can add it to your phone's calendar so it actually happens.
Do the kind thing. Then mark it done.
Keep your people close. Add the people who matter, with a note about what they love to do, so your plans feel personal.
Care for yourself, too. Self-care counts. Plan a walk, a quiet evening, or a break you've earned, right alongside your plans for others.
Find ideas when you're stuck. Browse kindness ideas by type: kind words, your time, small gifts, and acts of service.
Look beyond your circle. Find ideas for kindness toward neighbors, strangers, and your community.
Save ideas for later. Keep a list of ideas you want to come back to.
Kindness for every budget. Many ideas cost nothing at all.
Get gentle reminders. See upcoming plans on your dashboard, or choose to get reminders by email.
Look back on the good you've done. Tap Track What I've Done to see a monthly recap of the kindness you've shared with others and with yourself.

sections.heading: It's for you, not for likes.

blocks.text: Care About You isn't a social network. There are no followers, no public feeds, and no one keeping score. Your kindness stays between you and the people you care about. Your monthly recap is just for you, a quiet reminder of the good you're putting into the world.

“So many relationships today feel transactional. I built Care About You because I believe people would benefit from simple reminders to do kind things for others and for themselves. Small acts, done often, can change how we feel about each other and about ourselves.”
— Sam, Founder and Executive Director, Apps for Change

Your people, plans, and notes are private. They're stored securely in your account, never sold, and never used for ads. Care About You doesn't use AI. The app asks your permission before adding anything to your calendar, and it never reads your other events.
Tip: You don't need to share private details. A first name and a few words are enough.
How we protect your data

title: Beat the Craving | Apps for Change
description: Cravings pass. Beat the Craving puts your coping strategies one tap away, counts every craving you beat, and helps you learn your triggers. Free, private, and judgment-free.
headline: Cravings pass. You'll have a plan for every one.
body: The first weeks of recovery are the hardest, and cravings don't wait for a good time. Beat the Craving puts the coping strategies you trust one tap away, counts every craving you beat, and helps you see what sets them off. Your plan, ready when you need it.
label: Beat the Craving · Coming 2027
tagline: Free. No ads. Never sold. Built by a nonprofit, for you.

blocks.text: Need help right now? Go to crisis resources

items: A craving hits late at night, and nobody's around to talk you through it.
You know what helps. In the moment, it's hard to remember.
You're counting days, but the hard moments in between don't get counted at all.
You don't want another app that sends you notifications, judges you, or asks for money.

blocks.text: Willpower alone is a lot to ask. You need a plan you can reach in seconds. That's what Beat the Craving is for.

items: Open the app. Your coping strategies are right on the first screen. No menus to dig through.
Pick one and do it. Take a walk, breathe, call someone, pray, or reach for anything else on your list. Some strategies open straight to outside help, like calling or finding an AA meeting near you.
Count the win. Every time you choose a coping strategy instead, your counter goes up.
Learn your patterns. Note what set the craving off, and start to see when and where they tend to hit.

blocks.text: Beat the Craving comes with coping strategies people in recovery rely on:
Take a walk · Pray · Call a friend · Breathe · Play a game · Take a shower · Grounding exercise · Distraction game
Make it yours. Edit any strategy, remove what doesn't fit, and add the ones that work for you. Your toolkit should look like your recovery, not anyone else's.
Days in recovery
Watch your days add up on a simple counter.
Cravings beaten
Every craving you ride out is a win. Your counter goes up each time you choose a coping strategy, so you can see how much strength you've already shown.
Triggers and patterns

Log what was happening: the time, the place, how you felt, and who you were with, or write it in your own words. Over time, Beat the Craving shows your patterns, like cravings that hit most in the evening, so you can plan ahead for them.

sections.heading: No notifications. No AI. No judgment.

items: No notifications, ever. Beat the Craving never sends alerts, so nothing about your recovery pops up on your lock screen.
No AI, by design. Everything in the app comes from you: your strategies, your words, your plan.
Any path to recovery. 12-step, faith-based, counseling, medication-assisted treatment, or cutting back. Beat the Craving works alongside whatever is working for you.
Alcohol, nicotine, or other drugs. If cravings are part of your story, this app is for you.

sections.heading: Free for good. Private for good.

blocks.text: Beat the Craving is made by Apps for Change, a Minnesota 501(c)(3) nonprofit. Help should never sit behind a paywall, and your recovery should never be someone else's business.

items: Free. No trials, no premium tier, no paywall. Every tool is free, including crisis resources.
No ads. Ever.
Treated as sensitive. What you enter is stored securely in your account and never sold, never used for ads, and never shared with employers, insurers, funders, or partner organizations.
Yours to control. Our team doesn't read your entries, and you can delete them anytime.

blocks.text: How we protect your data
Beat the Craving is a self-help tool. It isn't addiction treatment, and it doesn't replace care from a doctor, counselor, or recovery program.

blocks.question: How much does Beat the Craving cost?
blocks.text: Nothing, now or later. It's free because we're a nonprofit funded by donations, not by our users.

blocks.question: Does it work with my recovery program?
blocks.text: Yes. Beat the Craving doesn't follow one method. Use it alongside a 12-step group, your faith, counseling, medication-assisted treatment, or your own plan to cut back.

blocks.question: Will anyone know I'm using it?
blocks.text: The app never sends notifications, and we never share your entries with anyone. Beat the Craving doesn't have its own passcode, so keep your phone's lock screen turned on.

blocks.question: Is this a replacement for treatment?
blocks.text: No. It's a self-help tool for hard moments. If you need treatment, call SAMHSA's National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357 for free, confidential referrals, 24/7.

title: Advocate's Compass | Apps for Change
description: Speaking up for yourself isn't always easy, especially with a doctor, a landlord, a boss, or a room full of professionals making decisions about your life. Advocate's Compass helps you learn the skills, find the words, and walk in prepared.
headline: Know what to say when it matters most.
body: Speaking up for yourself isn't always easy, especially with a doctor, a landlord, a boss, or a room full of professionals making decisions about your life. Advocate's Compass helps you learn the skills, find the words, and walk in prepared.
label: Advocate's Compass · Coming 2027

blocks.text: People with disabilities, people navigating services and systems, caregivers and family members, and anyone who has left a meeting thinking, "I wish I'd said that."

items: Learn at your own pace. Short lessons on knowing your rights, communicating clearly, and preparing for the conversations that matter.
Practice real situations. Work through common scenarios so you feel ready when they happen.
Find the words with Advocate Now. Describe your situation, and AI writes a script you can use: what to say, what to ask, and how to follow up. Edit it until it sounds like you.
Prepare for meetings. Keep track of upcoming meetings and list what you want to say and ask.
Take notes and follow up. Write down what was decided, who will do what, and what happens next.
See your progress. Track the lessons you've finished and the skills you've built.
Asking a doctor for a second opinion
Asking a landlord for a repair
Requesting an accommodation at work
Speaking up in a support planning meeting
Questioning a bill or a denied benefit
Advocating for your child at school

blocks.text: Advocate's Compass grew out of years of experience in Minnesota human services. We saw how often people needed better tools to plan their own lives and speak up for themselves.

Advocate Now uses AI to write scripts. When you ask for one, what you type is sent to our AI service provider to create it. It's never sold or used for ads. Scripts are a starting point. You know your situation best.
Advocate's Compass offers general education and practice tools, not legal advice. For legal questions, talk with a lawyer or a legal aid organization.
How we protect your data

title: Your Data, Your Choice | Apps for Change
description: Our apps are free, ad-free, and never sell your data. Here's how we store, protect, and delete your information, in plain language.
headline: Your data. Your choice.
body: Many free apps make money by selling your information or showing you ads. We don't do either, and we never will. As a nonprofit with no owners, we have no reason to.

items: Sell your information, to anyone, ever.
Use it for advertising.
Share it with employers, insurers, funders, or partner organizations.
Track you for advertising, in our apps or on this website.
Put features behind a paywall.

rows: Your account, on our secure cloud servers
Your account, on our secure cloud servers
Your account, on our secure cloud servers
Your account, on our secure cloud servers

blocks.text: Your account means your information is there when you get a new phone or use more than one device.

Only what each app needs to work: your email and a name or username for your account, the entries you create, and basic technical details like device type and crash reports. We don't collect your precise location, and we don't build advertising profiles. Goal Getter and Care About You ask your permission before adding anything to your calendar.

Our team doesn't read your entries. The only exceptions are when you ask us for help with a support issue, when the law requires it, or when we need to investigate a security problem. Trusted service providers, like our cloud host, store information for us under written agreements that let them use it only to run our apps.
Your information is encrypted while it travels between your device and our servers. Access is limited to the few people who operate and support the apps.

Only one app uses AI, and only when you ask. In Advocate's Compass, asking Advocate Now for a script sends what you type to our AI service provider. Goal Getter, Care About You, and Beat the Craving don't use AI at all.
Entries in Beat the Craving may relate to recovery, substance use, or emotional well-being. We treat them as sensitive and protect them that way.

items: Delete any entry inside the app at any time.
Delete your whole account in the app's settings, or by emailing support@appsforchange.org. We remove it from our active systems within 30 days and from backups within 90 days.
Uninstalling an app doesn't delete your account. To erase your information, delete your account.

blocks.text: When we tell funders and our Board how we're doing, we use only totals, like the number of people using our apps. We never share anyone's individual entries.
Our apps are for people 13 and older. If you're under 18, please use them with a parent's or guardian's involvement.
Read our full Privacy Policy
Or email support@appsforchange.org.

title: About Us | Apps for Change
description: Apps for Change is a Minnesota 501(c)(3) nonprofit building free, private apps that help people reach goals, care for others, and advocate for themselves.
headline: Free tools for a better life, built with the people who use them.

blocks.text: Apps for Change develops free mobile apps, educational tools, and community programs that promote self-advocacy, goal achievement, personal resilience, caregiver support, and community engagement. Our work aims to reduce poverty, dependence, and social despair. Every app and program is free.

sections.heading: Why I started Apps for Change

blocks.text: "I started Apps for Change because it was the most realistic way for me to make a difference in my community.

Before this, I spent years in Minnesota human services, working alongside people navigating disability, recovery, and complex support systems. I saw how often people needed simple, practical tools to plan their own lives and speak up for themselves.
I want people to have a free app that can help them improve their life. No strings attached."
— Sam, Founder and Executive Director

Apps for Change began as a personal development framework built around eight areas of a balanced life: relationships, purpose, physical health, learning, service, environment, emotional well-being, and finances. What started as worksheets grew into digital tools.

Along the way, we saw gaps in Minnesota's disability services, where people needed better support for self-advocacy and clearer ways to plan their own lives. We built apps to fill those gaps, and the work grew from there.

items: Free means free. No ads, subscriptions, in-app purchases, or paywalls.
Privacy comes first. Your information is never sold or used for ads.
Independence over dependence. Technology should build your strength, not keep you scrolling. Every feature answers one question: does this help someone take the next step on their own?
Built with community. The people who use our apps help shape them.
Everyone belongs. We build for people of every background and ability, including people who don't consider themselves "tech people."

blocks.text: Apps for Change is a Minnesota nonprofit corporation and a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, EIN 41-4014098.

items: Governed by a three-member Board of Directors that meets at least four times a year
Bylaws that require input from community town halls to go to the Board
No owners or shareholders. If we ever close, our bylaws require any remaining assets to go to other 501(c)(3) nonprofits or a public body, never to an individual.

blocks.text: Our bylaws, policies, and financial information are available on request at info@appsforchange.org.

The need is large. In 2024, 48.4 million people in the U.S. aged 12 and older had a substance use disorder in the past year. Of those who needed substance use treatment, only about 1 in 5 received it.
SAMHSA, 2024 National Survey on Drug Use and Health.

blocks.question: Do you sell my data?
Which apps use AI?
blocks.text: Only Advocate's Compass, for Advocate Now scripts, and only when you ask for one. Goal Getter, Care About You, and Beat the Craving don't use AI.

blocks.question: How do I delete my information?
blocks.text: Delete any entry in the app anytime. To delete your whole account, use the app's settings or email support@appsforchange.org. Uninstalling an app doesn't delete your account.

blocks.question: Is Beat the Craving a treatment program?
blocks.text: No. It's a self-help tool. It isn't addiction treatment and doesn't replace a doctor, counselor, or recovery program.

blocks.question: Who can use the apps?
blocks.text: People 13 and older. If you're under 18, please use them with a parent's or guardian's involvement.

blocks.question: Can you help with accessibility needs?
blocks.text: Yes. Tell us what you need at support@appsforchange.org and we'll do our best to help.
Email info@appsforchange.org, or bring it to a town hall
blocks.question: I have an app idea. Where do I send it?
Can my organization use your apps?
blocks.text: We'd love to talk. Email info@appsforchange.org.
